weeks.summary: A tooling-heavy week: two major E2E runners shipped flakiness features independently, and the industry survey data backfilled a trend that's been visible anecdotally for a year — QA is now writing evals, not just test cases.

items.title: Playwright 1.48 ships built-in flaky-test quarantine
items.summary: Failing tests can now be auto-tagged and re-run in isolation instead of blocking the whole suite.

items.title: Survey: 61% of QA teams now maintain an internal LLM eval suite
items.summary: Eval-writing overtook manual exploratory testing as a stated primary duty for the first time.

items.title: Kubernetes 1.32 stabilizes in-place pod resource resizing
items.summary: Long-running test environments can be resized without a pod restart, cutting a common source of E2E flakiness.

weeks.summary: Quieter week dominated by a single essay on shift-left fatigue that generated more discussion than any release did.

items.title: Why 'shift-left' quietly became 'shift-everywhere' in 2026
items.summary: Testing responsibilities spread across the whole delivery pipeline instead of just moving earlier in it.

items.title: Postman adds contract-testing mode against OpenAPI specs
items.summary: Collections can be validated against a live OpenAPI schema on every run.
